cohort_name: [DVI] Major Lower Extremity Amputation (dysvascular, trauma/cancer excluded)
logic_description: TARGET (this study's own, replacing shared 1797941 as of 2026-08-12). Identical entry event and age rule to [DVI] Major Lower Extremity Amputation (1797941), which this study previously used, with three deliberate changes -- all made in a NEW cohort because 1797941 is shared VERBATIM with pad-amp-ed-desc, a merged and PRCC-verified study whose target population must not shift. (1) LE-wound concept set broadened 5 -> 24 ancestors, restoring the definition pad-amp-nhd-val used (ulcers, open wounds, the fragmented gangrene trees, cellulitis, osteomyelitis, diabetic foot). All 24 [vocab query] re-verified 2026-08-12 (SNOMED 2025-02-01 Intl / 2025-03-01 US): standard='S', valid, domain='Condition'. nhd-val listed 25; 4263116 'Gangrene' is OMITTED because it is domain_id='Observation' and can never match a Condition criterion -- it was equally inert in nhd-val's condition_occurrence query. (2) Indication evaluated against condition_occurrence, NOT condition_era, and PER-INDICATION WINDOWS replace 1797941's unbounded one (tightened 2026-08-12): PAD and DM = any time prior through +365d; LE wound = -365d through +365d. Rationale: PAD and DM are chronic, so any prior record counts, and the window extends forward because the amputation admission is frequently where PAD is first formally coded; a wound is an acute episode, so it is bracketed to +/-1yr -- a wound five years earlier is not this amputation's indication. 1797941 accepted an indication coded at ANY time including years AFTER the amputation; nhd-val required it on or before index. This sits between the two, deliberately. Windows verified to bind: narrowing all three to +/-1d yields ZERO patients on synthetic data, and the rendered SQL carries 1x DATEADD(day,-365,..) (wound lower bound) and 3x DATEADD(day,365,..) (all three upper bounds). condition_era is a DERIVED table; on the real Duke CDM this cohort found ~60 fewer amputations than nhd-val, which read condition_occurrence, and a partially-built era table is the leading explanation. NOTE: on synthetic data (1)+(2) together change the count by ZERO (176 -> 176), so synthetic cannot validate the recovery -- only a Duke re-run can. (3) NEW exclusion 'No trauma or malignancy indication': zero traumatic-amputation (4096479 [vocab query], 165 std desc) and zero malignant-neoplasm (443392 [vocab query], reused from the verified phenotype_library catalog entry malignant_neoplasm) condition records within +/-30d of the index admission. INDICATION-ANCHORED BY DESIGN, not an all-time history exclusion: the question is whether THIS amputation was for trauma or cancer, and an all-time rule would drop legitimate diabetic-foot amputations for a decades-old fracture or remote cancer history. nhd-val excluded these causes only IMPLICITLY, via the dysvascular indication requirement, so this is a new criterion rather than a restored one. Removes 6 of 176 on synthetic data. alignment_status: LOCAL ONLY -- not in ATLAS; named [DVI] from the start per the workspace convention so pushing it upstream is not a rename exercise. UPDATED 2026-08-12 (second Duke run): the combined trauma-or-malignancy rule excluded 302 of 935 patients (32%) -- implausible for a dysvascular cohort, and the inclusion bitmask resolves only to whole rules so trauma and malignancy could not be attributed separately. Now TWO rules. Trauma keeps the +/-30d window and is not visit-restricted (it may be coded on a preceding ED or transfer encounter). Malignancy is now RestrictVisit -- attached to the index inpatient visit only, the same mechanism the nested amputation criterion uses -- so it asks whether THIS admission's amputation was for cancer rather than whether the patient has a cancer code in the same month. On synthetic data this returns the cohort to 176 (from 170) while remaining demonstrably live rather than inert: that CDM has condition_occurrence.visit_occurrence_id populated 99.9% and 220 persons with a malignancy, yet none attached to an index amputation admission. IF THE DUKE RUN NOW EXCLUDES ~0 FOR MALIGNANCY, check that fill rate before concluding there is no cancer -- an unpopulated visit_occurrence_id makes any visit-restricted criterion match nothing, silently. MALIGNANCY SET NARROWED 2026-08-12: 443392 'Malignant neoplastic disease' (5,314 std descendants, all cancers all sites) -> 4177242 'Malignant tumor of lower limb' (250), a 21x tightening to the anatomy that causes a lower-extremity amputation. Verified by concept_ancestor that 4177242 subsumes the bone (4162138), soft-tissue (37166992), skin (4162993) and primary-neoplasm (201518) lower-limb variants, so one concept covers the anatomy. Registered in phenotype_library/catalog.yaml as malignant_tumor_lower_limb. ACCEPTED GAP: a sarcoma coded with no site sits outside this tree. 'Attached to the amputation procedure' was requested and is NOT possible -- condition_occurrence carries no procedure link in OMOP (only visit_occurrence_id / visit_detail_id), so the visit is the finest scope available. TRAUMA WINDOW CHANGED 2026-08-12 (third Duke run): the +/-30d trauma rule excluded 220 of 935 (24%) while the visit-scoped malignancy rule excluded only 17 -- the reverse of what was predicted. 220 traumatic amputations is not credible in a cohort already filtered to PAD/DM/wound (all 220 had passed that rule), and this concept's descendants are 'Traumatic amputation above knee / below knee / of foot', which is how a coder may describe the SURGICAL amputation just performed. The window is now [-30d, -1d], strictly before the admission: genuine trauma precedes the amputation, a miscode of the surgery appears on or after it. circe has no 'NOT at this visit' operator so the index encounter cannot be excluded directly. The next run is therefore a TEST: a collapse from 220 to a small number confirms the miscoding hypothesis; staying near 220 means the trauma genuinely precedes the admission. Accepted cost: same-day trauma-to-amputation is no longer excluded. TRAUMA RULE REPLACED 2026-08-12 (after the third Duke run): 4096479 'Traumatic amputation' -> a 5-concept MECHANISM set (crushing injury of lower limb 194229 / of foot 72487, burn of lower limb 197751, degloving 4095264, fracture of lower limb 4187096), all [vocab query] verified 2026-08-12, and scoped to the index visit (RestrictVisit) rather than a day window. WHY: the old concept's descendants name the amputation ('Traumatic amputation above/below knee, of foot'), the same words a coder may use for the surgery just performed, so a +/-30d window excluded 220 of 935 (24%) who had all already met the dysvascular indication. Mechanism concepts cannot be confused with a surgical amputation, so the criterion can sit ON the admission where the signal is strongest. GENERAL injury ancestors were measured and rejected -- SNOMED files open wounds under injuries, so 440921 'Traumatic injury' shares 888 of our 1,372 wound concepts and 4130852 'Injury of lower limb' shares 982; either would exclude the dysvascular patients this study is about. Registered as limb_trauma_mechanism in phenotype_library/catalog.yaml.
